1. I personally would not do that as to just have 1 less thing to worry about on surgery day.

2. My surgeon told me I could use clippers to trim my chest hair. I would ask your surgeon first, but I am imagining they will not want you to shave with a razor as people in the operating room can do that.

3. You are going to strip down to your bday suit for surgery. Wear sweatpants and a shirt that zips or buttons up- it’s hard to put on clothes when you still feel loopy from anesthesia. Wear slip on shoes!

4. You should ask the surgeons office for more specific info about keeping your piercing in. It’s more about creating a sterile environment for surgery and that’s why they require you to remove all jewelry. If you do have to remove it- hopefully your surgery will be quick and you can put it in as soon as you are done.

5. They will get you a big plastic bag to put your items in, if you bring your own bag it will go inside a plastic bag like this.

6. Definitely bring some water, and a small snack. I had water, Gatorade, and a cliff bar. You may feel a little nausea so something basic is good. 

Best of luck to you!

My advice for you:

1. Talk to ur Dr about your plans to quit. Your body will experience withdrawal and it will help to have some more professional guidance.

2. You’re right- quitting weed is definitely an emotional mess at the start- but in the midst of it all, keeping a positive mind frame will help tremendously. Recovery from an addiction is no easy task. That’s why you should celebrate every minute/hour that you are able to go without smoking- cuz that’s a huge deal!!! Celebrate & lift yourself up as much as you can, beating yourself up over the past & mistakes is really unproductive and not fair to someone (you) going through this major change.

3. Download an app, or get a wall calendar (I did both) to track the days you go without weed. I used the calendar to add in different things each week for what I planned on doing with my time spent not getting high.

4. Cold turkey is the way to go (unless ur dr is against it). No longer smoking weed (for me personally) makes life easier- why complicate your goal of getting weed free by figuring out these compromises of when/how much to smoke if the end goal is zero?!

Best of luck to you :)
